title: Atlas Crossing Partners FY2023 Annual LP Report — Fund III
summary: Annual LP report for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III covering the year ended December 31, 2023. Fund III is a $420M fully committed vehicle with five active platform companies (Wholesum Foods, Crestview Coffee, Vanguard Auto Parts, Pinecrest Foods, Forgelight Manufacturing) and one full exit (Brightline Industrial to Parker Hannifin at 2.4× MOIC / 22.1% gross IRR). Aggregate portfolio revenue reached $428M (+9.5% YoY) and EBITDA $62.8M (+10.0%). Fund-level metrics: gross IRR 19.8%, gross MOIC 1.72×, net IRR 15.9% (est.), TVPI 1.65×, DPI 0.32×, NAV $218.4M at year-end. Cumulative distributions of $120.5M were driven by the Brightline exit ($68.4M) and a Wholesum partial recap ($52.1M). Key FY2024 priorities include commencing the Wholesum exit process, closing the Vanguard Tri-State Parts add-on, reducing leverage at Crestview, and beginning Fund IV LP outreach. Audited by Deloitte & Touche LLP (unqualified opinion).

key_quotes.quote: The headline story of FY2023 was the sale of Brightline Industrial to Parker Hannifin, which closed in June 2023 at a 2.4× MOIC and 22.1% gross IRR. This was Fund III's first full exit and returned $68.4M to limited partners in Q4 2023.
key_quotes.topic: FY2023 first full exit — Brightline Industrial

key_quotes.quote: Both events brought cumulative Fund III distributions to $120.5M against $371.2M called, for a DPI of 0.32× at year-end.
Our portfolio companies with floating-rate debt (Wholesum, Vanguard) saw $3.8M of incremental annual interest expense vs. our 2021 underwrite models.
key_quotes.topic: Macro and interest rate environment impact

key_quotes.quote: Year-end leverage 11.4× EBITDA. Board approved accelerated debt paydown plan: $7–9M annual FCF directed to mandatory amortization. Target sub-10× by FY2025.
Year-end EBITDA margin 17.0% vs. 15.8% at underwriting. Benefit from direct materials sourcing renegotiation completed Q2 2023 ($0.4M annual savings).

growth_drivers: Organic portfolio revenue growth (+9.5% YoY)
Geographic expansion at Crestview Coffee (31 new locations)
Proprietary SKU mix expansion at Vanguard Auto Parts
Add-on acquisition strategy (Pacific Harvest, Tri-State Parts pipeline)
New distribution hub and OEM relationships at portfolio companies
risks: Elevated interest rate environment increasing debt service costs ($3.8M incremental interest expense vs. underwrite)
High leverage at Crestview Coffee (11.4× EBITDA) and Pinecrest Foods (34.8×)
Commodity input cost inflation (palm oil, dairy, packaging)
Customer concentration at Pinecrest Foods (top customer 38% of revenue)
Slower M&A market impacting exit timing and valuation multiples

title: Atlas Crossing Partners — FY2024 Annual LP Report (Fund III)
summary: Annual LP Report for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III covering the year ended December 31, 2024, audited by Deloitte & Touche LLP. Fund III is a $420M fully-committed lower-middle-market buyout fund with a gross IRR of 20.9%, net IRR of ~16.9%, and TVPI/Gross MOIC of 1.88×. DPI reached 0.62× on $230.1M in cumulative distributions. FY2024 featured two major capital return events: the second Wholesum Foods dividend recap ($49.8M) and the exit of Meridian Facility Management to Warburg Pincus ($59.8M). Active portfolio companies include Wholesum Foods (food distribution), Crestview Coffee (specialty beverage/QSR), Vanguard Auto Parts (auto distribution), Pinecrest Foods (specialty food ingredients), and Forgelight Manufacturing (light industrial). Aggregate portfolio revenue grew 10.3% YoY to $461M; aggregate EBITDA grew 7.3% to $66.4M. Key FY2025 priorities: Wholesum exit process (Goldman Sachs engaged), Tri-State Parts bolt-on close for Vanguard, and Fund IV launch targeted H1 2026.

key_quotes.quote: Two significant events defined the year from a capital return standpoint: (1) a second partial recapitalization of Wholesum Foods in Q3 2024 returning $49.8M to LPs; and (2) the sale of Meridian Facility Management (a Fund II asset completing its runoff) contributing $59.8M in Q4 2024. Total Fund III distributions for FY2024 were $109.6M, bringing our cumulative DPI to 0.62× as of December 31, 2024.

Cumulative Wholesum distributions $101.9M — exceeding original equity invested of $75.25M. QofE finalized Q4 2024. Goldman Sachs selected as sell-side banker; formal process expected Q2–Q3 2025 (subsequently delayed to Q2 2026).
Revenue of $140.2M vs. plan of $138M. Driven by fleet account wins (4 contracts, $3.8M annualized) and proprietary SKU mix expansion to 37%.

Lower-MM M&A volume recovered modestly (+8% vs. 2023) but remained well below 2021 peak. Key dynamic: growing inventory of processes from founders who deferred exits during 2022–2023 rate environment. We saw 52 new opportunities in 2024 (vs. 41 in 2023), with a higher proportion of proprietary introductions (42%).

growth_drivers: Input cost relief benefiting Pinecrest Foods and Wholesum
Vanguard Auto fleet account wins and proprietary SKU expansion
Crestview Coffee system location expansion (+38 new locations)
Add-on strategy — Tri-State Parts LOI for Vanguard
Pacific Harvest integration driving Wholesum revenue growth
risks: High leverage at Crestview Coffee (10.8× net leverage)
Customer concentration at Pinecrest Foods (34% top customer)
Tariff uncertainty on imported food ingredients
Pinecrest commodity exposure (palm oil, sunflower)
Wholesale/secondary exit timing risk for Wholesum

title: Atlas Crossing Partners — Q1 2026 LP Quarterly Report (Fund III)
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners' Q1 2026 LP Quarterly Report for Fund III (vintage 2020, $420M committed, fully called). As of March 31, 2026, the fund reports Gross IRR of 21.4%, Gross MOIC of 1.94×, Net IRR of 17.6%, DPI of 0.62×, TVPI of 1.94×, and closing NAV of $252.4M. The portfolio comprises five active platforms — Wholesum Foods (specialty food distribution), Crestview Coffee (QSR/specialty beverage), Vanguard Auto Parts (specialty auto distribution), Pinecrest Foods (specialty food ingredients), and Forgelight Manufacturing (light industrial). Aggregate LTM revenue of $512M grew 11.4% YoY; aggregate LTM EBITDA of $74M grew 9.8%. Wholesum Foods is in active exit preparation (QofE complete, Goldman Sachs engaged, formal process expected Q2–Q3 2026). Vanguard Auto Parts crossed $200M annualized revenue ahead of schedule. Forgelight Manufacturing signed an add-on LOI (Project Kestrel, $31M EV). Fund IV fundraise at $168M committed (42% of $400M target); first close targeted August 2026. Cumulative LP distributions total $230.1M.

key_quotes.quote: We completed a comprehensive sell-side Quality of Earnings process in Q4 2025 and are in advanced discussions with potential buyers and strategic partners. We expect to provide an update on Wholesum's exit trajectory by Q2 2026.
Vanguard Auto Parts delivered its strongest quarter to date, crossing $200M in annualized revenue for the first time, ahead of our underwriting schedule by approximately two quarters.
Active holdings marked at cost or last-round valuation; partially realized (Wholesum recap Oct 2024) at exit proceeds.
Seller multiples in our core sectors (Business Services, Spec. Distribution) remain compressed vs. 2021 peaks — we are seeing processes clearing at 8.5–10.5× EBITDA vs. 11–14× in 2021.
We have commitments of $168M (42% of target) as of May 2026. We expect to hold a first close in August and are grateful for the LP re-up support we have received.

growth_drivers: Organic revenue growth across all five portfolio platforms (+11.4% YoY aggregate)
Wholesum Foods new SKU launches and geographic distribution expansion
Vanguard Auto Parts crossing $200M annualized revenue; Tri-State Parts add-on integration
Crestview Coffee same-store sales growth (+8.4%) and new market expansion (22 states)
Forgelight Manufacturing margin expansion and add-on LOI (Project Kestrel)
risks: Labor inflation (~3.8% weighted basis) above original underwriting assumptions
High leverage across several portfolio companies (Vanguard 11.1×, Forgelight 18.3×, Crestview 9.7×)
Wholesum Foods exit outcome uncertainty; actual proceeds may differ materially from scenarios
Commodity cost exposure at Pinecrest Foods (palm oil, sunflower)
MOIC (1.94×) and EBITDA growth (1.6× avg.) currently tracking below underwriting targets (2.5–3.0× and 2.2× respectively)

title: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III — Q3 2025 LP Quarterly Report
summary: LP Quarterly Report for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III as of September 30, 2025. Fund III is fully committed at $420M with a Gross IRR of 20.6%, Gross MOIC of 1.86×, Net IRR of 16.8%, DPI of 0.62×, and closing NAV of $237.2M. The portfolio consists of five active platforms: Wholesum Foods (specialty food distribution), Crestview Coffee (QSR/specialty beverage), Vanguard Auto Parts (specialty auto distribution), Pinecrest Foods (specialty food ingredients), and Forgelight Manufacturing (light industrial). Aggregate LTM revenue across the portfolio is $488M with $69M EBITDA at a 14.1% margin. Key Q3 activities include the signing of a Tri-State Parts LOI (Vanguard add-on, $28M EV), ongoing Pacific Harvest integration at Wholesum, and exit preparation commenced for Wholesum. Fund IV fundraise is planned for H1 2026. Macro commentary highlights a 25bps Fed rate cut in September 2025 and improving M&A conditions in the lower-middle market.

key_quotes.quote: Gross IRR 20.6% (Underwrite: 22–25%, Tracking); Gross MOIC 1.86× (Underwrite: 2.5–3.0×, On-track); Net IRR 16.8% (Underwrite: 18–21%, Tracking).
Exit preparation begun — Engaged QofE advisor (EY) for sell-side quality of earnings. No external process launched; expect to select banker Q4 2025 / Q1 2026.
Net leverage at 10.7× EBITDA. Strong FCF generation ($8.4M TTM) being directed to mandatory amortization; targeting 9.5× by end of FY2026.

Sponsor-to-sponsor and sponsor-to-strategic deal volume up 11% in Q3 2025 vs. Q3 2024 per Pitchbook. Lower-middle-market ($75–300M EV) remains less competitive than large-cap — we are consistently seeing 3–5 credible bidders in processes vs. 8–12 in 2021.
In preparation for Fund IV fundraise (launch H1 2026), we have begun LP relationship reactivation and are seeing strong re-up intent from Fund I–III investors.

growth_drivers: Geographic expansion (Crestview Coffee — 33 new locations YTD)
Add-on acquisitions (Tri-State Parts LOI, Pacific Harvest integration)
Organic revenue growth across Vanguard Auto (+8.1%) and Forgelight (+4.8%)
Digital loyalty channel growth at Crestview Coffee (1.1M members, 27% of system sales)
New OEM contracts at Forgelight Manufacturing ($2.1M combined annualized revenue)
Proprietary SKU mix expansion at Vanguard Auto
risks: Elevated leverage across multiple portfolio companies (Crestview 10.7×, Vanguard 12.7×, Forgelight 19.1×)
Input cost inflation at Wholesum Foods (~4.2% YoY, net 40bps EBITDA margin impact)
Customer concentration at Pinecrest Foods (top customer 31% of revenue)
Commodity exposure at Pinecrest Foods (palm/sunflower oil prices)
Potential tariff expansion on imported raw materials (Pinecrest Foods inputs)
Returns tracking below underwritten case (Gross IRR 20.6% vs. 22–25% UW; MOIC 1.86× vs. 2.5–3.0× UW)

title: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III — Q4 2025 LP Quarterly Report
summary: LP Quarterly Report for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund III as of Q4 2025 (quarter ended December 31, 2025). The $420M fund is fully committed with a Gross IRR of 21.1%, Gross MOIC of 1.90×, Net IRR of 17.2%, DPI of 0.62×, and TVPI of 1.90×. Closing NAV was $246.2M with cumulative distributions of $230.1M. The fund holds five active platforms: Wholesum Foods (food distribution, in sell-side process), Crestview Coffee (QSR/specialty beverage, deleveraging), Vanguard Auto Parts (specialty auto distribution, post-Tri-State integration), Pinecrest Foods (specialty food ingredients), and Forgelight Manufacturing (light industrial, LOI signed for bolt-on). Aggregate portfolio LTM revenue was $499M and LTM EBITDA was $71M (14.2% margin). Fund IV launch is set for February 2026 with a target first close of $150–200M.

key_quotes.quote: Gross MOIC 2.5–3.0× [underwrite], 1.90× [current], On-track. Net IRR 18–21% [underwrite], 17.2% [current], Tracking.
GS engaged as sell-side M&A advisor in November 2025. CIM preparation underway; formal process expected Q2–Q3 2026.

The most notable dynamic: a meaningful increase in founder/family-owned business processes as sellers who delayed in 2022–2023 (awaiting better terms) are now coming to market. This plays to our proprietary sourcing strength.

Fund IV formal launch set for February 2026. PPM has been circulated to select LP prospects for review. Re-up LPs from Fund III will be given a 30-day priority window ahead of any first close. Target first close: $150–200M by August 2026.
All five Fund III platforms closed FY2025 at or ahead of internal plan. Aggregate EBITDA growth of 9.2% YoY reflects continued organic expansion and the Tri-State Parts contribution.

growth_drivers: Organic expansion across five platforms
Add-on acquisitions (Tri-State Parts closed Q4 2025, Forgelight bolt-on LOI signed)
OEM contract ramp at Forgelight
New CPG accounts at Pinecrest
Crestview store expansion (42 new locations in FY2025)
Wholesum Foods exit process initiated with Goldman Sachs as sell-side advisor
risks: High leverage across portfolio (Vanguard 12.3×, Pinecrest 31.1×, Forgelight 18.9×, Crestview 10.3×)
Integration risk from Tri-State Parts acquisition
Wholesum Foods exit timeline execution risk
Commodity input cost exposure at Pinecrest Foods
Returns tracking below underwrite targets (Gross MOIC 1.90× vs. 2.5–3.0× UW)

title: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund IV — LP Presentation
summary: LP pitch deck for Atlas Crossing Partners Fund IV, a Chicago-based middle-market buyout fund targeting $400M ($450M hard cap) with a first close targeted August 2026 and final close February 2027. The fund continues the firm's strategy from Funds I–III: control buyouts of lower-middle-market businesses ($75–400M EV, $10–50M EBITDA) in Business Services, Specialty Distribution, and Industrial/Light Manufacturing. As of May 2026, $168M (42% of target) has been committed. The deck covers firm history (founded 2012, $910M raised across Funds I–III), investment team, track record (25.8% weighted gross IRR, 2.6× gross MOIC across all funds), active Fund III portfolio, Fund IV structure and terms (2.0% mgmt fee, 20% carry over 8% hurdle), value creation methodology, and current pipeline (3 deals in active diligence). Target gross IRR of 22–28% and gross MOIC of 2.5–3.5×.

key_quotes.quote: We operate as a true sector-agnostic-within-thesis firm — we do not chase macro cycles. Our edge is operational: we put the right operating executive in place within the first 90 days and run a structured Value Creation Plan for every holding.

Average EBITDA growth across Fund I–III platforms: 2.1× from entry to exit. Average hold-period entry multiple: 9.4×. Average exit multiple: 10.8×. The spread is real, but operational improvement drives the majority of value creation.
Rate environment has compressed seller multiples in the lower-middle-market; 2025–2027 vintage expected to benefit from reduced competition from large-cap PE.
38% of deals in the last 24 months were either proprietary or limited auction with ≤3 bidders. We consistently win deals at lower multiples than marketed processes.
GP commits ≥3% ($12M+) from personal capital. The entire investment team participates in carried interest. No key-person events; zero senior departures in 14 years. We eat what we cook.

growth_drivers: Proprietary and limited-auction sourcing (38% of deals) reducing competition and entry multiples
Market dislocation in lower-middle-market creating favorable entry pricing (2025–2027 vintage)
Operational value creation via 100-day plans, operating partner placement, and add-on M&A (avg. 1.8 add-ons per platform)
EBITDA margin expansion of 200–400 bps per platform targeted
Deep LP re-up base providing fundraising momentum
risks: Unrealized Fund III holdings (3 of 5 platforms not yet exited) carry mark-to-market risk
Fund IV fundraise still in progress at 42% of target as of May 2026
Hold period risk given active portfolio average hold already 4–8 years
Integration risk from add-on acquisition strategy
Key-person dependency on co-founders Michael Tang and Simon Harrington
